'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Iran–Israel proxy conflict]]
**[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]]
***[[April 2024 Iranian strikes on Israel|2024 Iranian strikes in Israel]], [[Iran–Japan relations]]
****[[Japan]] increases its four-stage danger ranking level for most of [[Iran]], including [[Tehran]], to Level 3, which urges Japanese citizens to [[travel warning|avoid all travel]] to Iran. [https://japannews.yomiuri.co.jp/politics/politics-government/20240415-180512/ (''The Japan News'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***[[Siege of El Fasher|Battle of El Fasher]]
****At least nine civilians are killed and sixty others are injured in a renewed offensive by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] on the city of [[El Fasher]]. [https://sudanwarmonitor.com/p/c75 (Sudan War Monitor)]
****The [[Rapid Support Forces]] capture [[Mellit District|Mellit]], [[North Darfur]]. [https://sudanwarmonitor.com/p/9e5 (Sudan War Monitor)]
**[[Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Humanitarian impact of the Sudanese civil war]]
***Donors pledge more than 2 billion euros for humanitarian aid in [[Sudan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/france-germany-eu-mark-anniversary-sudan-war-with-funding-push-2024-04-15/ (Reuters)]
**[[Siege of El Obeid]]
***Five civilians are killed and ten others are injured in crossfire between the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] and Rapid Support Forces in the city of [[El Obeid]]. [https://sudanwarmonitor.com/p/0fe (Sudan War Monitor)]
**The [[Darfur Joint Protection Force|Joint Darfur Force]] declares war on the Rapid Support Forces and allies with the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]]. [https://sudanwarmonitor.com/p/darfur-joint-force-declares-war-on (Sudan War Monitor)]
**Clashes occur in Al-Madina Arab, [[Gezira State]], between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/heavy-fighting-rages-in-al-madina-arab-al-gazira-state (Radio Tamazuj)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] CEO [[Elon Musk]] announces that more than 10% of the company's global workforce will be laid off. [https://www.cnbc.com/2024/04/15/tesla-shares-dip-in-premarket-trade-on-global-layoff-reports.html (CNBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-lay-off-more-than-10-its-staff-electrek-reports-2024-04-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Lockheed Martin]] wins a $17 billion defense contract from the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] to develop [[anti-ballistic missile]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/lockheed-wins-us-missile-defense-contract-worth-17-bln-sources-say-2024-04-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Fifty-eight people have been killed in [[Tanzania]] and 13 people have been killed in [[Kenya]] in the past two weeks by flooding caused by torrential rains, with more than 125,000 people in coastal areas of [[East Africa]] affected by the flooding. Tanzania announces plans to construct fourteen [[dam]]s in an attempt to reduce the damage from future floods. [https://apnews.com/article/tanzania-flooding-600d49f681172e4d6ac5265dff1111fa (AP)]
*[[Lightning]] and heavy [[rain]]s have killed at least 49 people across [[Pakistan]] in the past three days, mainly [[Agriculture|farmers]] in the eastern [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab province]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-rains-lightning-weather-a8d8035be76856a1538eb347a18ed675 (AP)]
*The death toll from [[landslide]]s caused by torrential rain in [[Tana Toraja]], [[South Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]], increases to 20, after the last missing people are found dead. [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-sulawesi-toraja-landslide-c3a53989cd2f04de8318d170b6401c46 (AP)]
*A magnitude 6.5 [[List of earthquakes in 2024|earthquake]] strikes [[West New Britain Province]], [[Papua New Guinea]]. No damage or casualties are reported. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/magnitude-65-earthquake-rattles-papua-new-guinea-tsunami-109224973 (ABC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Sudan–United Kingdom relations]], [[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] sanctions Alkhaleej Bank and Al-Fakher Advanced Works, two companies financing the [[Rapid Support Forces]], and Red Rock Mining, which finances the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]]. [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/uk-imposes-sanctions-on-3-companies-linked-to-sudan-war (Radio Tamazuj)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Australian Parliament House sexual misconduct allegations]]
**Former [[Australia]]n political staffer [[Bruce Lehrmann]] loses his defamation case against [[Network 10]] and journalist [[Lisa Wilkinson]] for broadcasting an interview with Lehrmann's former coworker [[Brittany Higgins]] in which she claimed that Lehrmann raped her. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2024/apr/15/bruce-lehrmann-defamation-trial-judge-verdict-rape-brittany-higgins-parliament-house-ntwnfb (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2024 Wakeley church stabbing]]
**Four people are injured, including [[bishop]] [[Mar Mari Emmanuel]], in a [[mass stabbing]] at a [[church (building)|church]] in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]]. The perpetrator is arrested. A mob clashes with police outside the church while trying to attack the detained suspect. [https://www.skynews.com.au/australia-news/crime/four-people-stabbed-at-church-in-sydneys-west-with-early-vision-picturing-one-victim-as-a-christian-leader/news-story/7aac1c9961eac0b91f93021253d18e94 (Sky News Australia)]
*[[Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse]]
**A [[Federal judiciary of the United States|federal court]] in the [[U.S. state]] of [[Virginia]] hears the first claims by survivors of the [[Abu Ghraib prison]] in [[Iraq]]. Three detainees accuse the [[CACI]] for their role in the torture at the prison. [https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2024/04/12/20-years-later-abu-ghraib-detainees-get-their-day-in-us-court/ (''Military Times'')] [https://apnews.com/article/abu-ghraib-trial-iraq-virginia-9e6eae5c7ea05fac90d8541efdd15562 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**[[Tax Day protests]]
***Pro-Palestinian protests in the [[United States]] stop traffic on the [[Golden Gate Bridge]] and disrupt traffic to [[Seattle–Tacoma International Airport]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2024/04/15/gaza-israel-war-protests-bridges/ (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Lee Hsien Loong]] announces that he will resign as [[Prime Minister of Singapore]] on May 15 and will be succeeded by [[Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore|Deputy Prime Minister]] and [[Ministry of Finance (Singapore)#Ministers|Finance Minister]] [[Lawrence Wong]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/prime-minister-lee-hsien-loong-lawrence-wong-leadership-handover-4266031 (CNA)]
*Thousands of people protest against a controversial [[Foreign_agent#Georgia|foreign agent law]] in [[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]. Georgia's Interior Ministry reports at least 14 people have been detained. [[Georgian Dream]] parliamentary leader [[Mamuka Mdinaradze]] is punched during a debate in [[Parliament of Georgia|parliament]] by a member of the opposition. [https://www.dw.com/en/georgia-thousands-protest-russian-style-foreign-agent-law/a-68834983 (DW)]
